rounds.response:
Recap — recommended start config: 6 seats (agents) with unified email+chat, Shopify Plus app (order/customer view), TrailTrack connector (REST/webhooks), and key automations: FAQ bot for top 10 issues, macros for order lookups, auto‑tagging and SLA routing.  
Estimated monthly cost: mid‑tier plan + connector support and modest per‑ticket AI credits ≈ $650–$800/month (near your $700 target); expect a one‑time implementation/migration fee (typically low‑thousands, final after scoping TrailTrack).  
4–6 week rollout (high level): wk0–1 kickoff & access; wk2 connector build + Shopify app install; wk3 data migration (import 6–12 months) & automation setup; wk4 agent training, QA & tuning; wk5–6 polish and final cutover (recommend short write‑freeze of minutes–a few hours).  
Key risks/open questions: TrailTrack edge cases to test (API rate limits, pagination, webhook retries, custom fields/metafields); how connector errors/alerts surface and who owns incident response; potential automation/AI credit caps if you apply heavy per‑ticket AI; any custom TrailTrack endpoints we should review pre‑scope.  
Want this as a one‑page decision brief with line‑item pricing and a draft SOW for the TrailTrack connector to share with finance (I can send it now)?

rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Clarifying usage limits**

I think it’s better to frame this in relative terms. There's significant headroom for an FAQ bot and order lookups at a given volume, as long as per-ticket AI usage remains moderate. If more than 30-50% of tickets require intensive AI, things might get tricky, particularly with high-frequency bot interactions. We can also mention that alerts will notify when approaching thresholds, but without giving specific percentages. Automated alerts and dashboards will keep admins informed of usage and activity, ensuring smooth operation.
**Detailing webhook failure management**

For the TrailTrack connector, we log webhook failures and try to retry with backoff. Errors are surfaced to the admin UI, and relevant contacts, like the SRE, receive email alerts. Detection typically occurs within minutes to hours, with a standard process of retries leading to an alert for the integration owner. If issues persist, our integration team escalates the concern. Resolution usually takes hours to a couple of business days, depending on the cause. We can also offer preconfigured thresholds and health checks to enhance monitoring efficiency.
**Summarizing key details**

There's plenty of headroom for an FAQ bot, order lookups, and routing at about 2.5–3k per month. The main risk lies in heavy per-ticket AI usage or very high bot conversation volume; if these remain moderate, caps won't be hit in the first 6-12 months. The platform offers real-time usage dashboards and alerts to notify admins as they approach caps. For the TrailTrack connector, webhook failures are tracked, and automated retries happen with backoff. Detection is typically within minutes to hours, with resolution often within hours but complex issues may take 1-2 business days.

Short answer on headroom: at ~2.5–3k tickets/month you’ll have comfortable headroom for an FAQ bot + order lookups + routing/SLA on the mid‑tier plan so long as per‑ticket AI work is moderate (the main pressure point is heavy per‑ticket AI or very high-frequency bot conversations).  
How you’ll see it coming: we provide real‑time dashboards for bot runs, API/webhook calls and AI credits plus configurable threshold alerts (email/Slack) that notify admins before caps are hit so you can act before service is affected.  
TrailTrack connector monitoring: webhook failures are logged and auto‑retried with exponential backoff; persistent failures surface in the integrations dashboard and trigger alerts to the designated contacts (your dev + optional on‑call from our integrations team).  
Typical detection & fix path: issues are usually detected in minutes–hours via alerts or dashboard flags; resolution is often a quick retry/config change or a dev fix (hours) but can take up to 1–2 business days for complex root causes requiring coordinated fixes.
